hook_text: One panel on a shop roof runs the lights, a fridge and a phone-charging board that earns money. Then a cloud comes. Then night. Here is what happens, and the whole case for and against solar.
clip_script: Light knocks electrons loose in silicon and a built-in push sends them round a circuit; nothing is used up. Half a volt a cell, so panels stack cells in series, and a shadow on a few cells chokes the lot. For night: controller, battery, inverter. The cloud? Battery covers it. Night? Battery carries it. Three rainy days? Fridge off, then lights. For: free fuel, no smoke, twenty-five years, works anywhere, cheaper than new coal. Against: nothing at night or in winter, batteries dear and short-lived, big up-front cost, mined materials, land. Verdict: our cheapest, cleanest new power, but never alone.
visual_style: Whiteboard silicon sandwich with electrons leaping; a panel of cells stacks up; a spaza roof with a sun arc, a cloud and a battery gauge rising and falling; a two-column for-and-against list.
pacing: Cell physics, panel, system day, advantages, disadvantages, verdict.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write your balanced verdict on solar in three sentences.
